# 2009B Question 10 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Compare and contrast**]{.task-verb} the neonatal respiratory system with the adult.
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Compare and contrast**]{.task-verb} the systems in a table after defining the neonatal period. Distinguish absolute values from values indexed to weight or lung volume and connect differences to clinical implications.

::: {.structure-table}
| Feature | Neonate | Adult |
|---|---|---|
| Anatomy | | |
| Ventilation and Gas Exchange | | |
| Lung Volumes | | |
| Mechanics of Breathing | | |
| Pulmonary Circulation | | |
| Control of Breathing | | |
| Haemoglobin | | |
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**36%** of candidates passed this question.

The neonatal period is from 0-28 days and this question predominantly concerned term neonates. This is not a question about the transition from intra- to extrauterine life nor is it a question about the pathophysiology of prematurity.

This is a wide ranging question concerning many aspects of respiratory physiology:- physiologically relevant anatomy; ventilation and gas exchange; lung volumes; mechanics of breathing; pulmonary circulation; control of breathing; and haemoglobin. The low pass rate resulted from most candidates not producing enough relevant detail in each of these areas.

Differences and similarities are both absolute (neonates are small) and relative (values indexed to weight or FRC). Mention of clinical implications gained extra marks. Well organised answers were frequently in a table form.
:::
